# How To Get More Accurate Search Volume Data In Google Keyword Planner

Paudy Heal

Posted 22 August, 2016 by [Paudy Heal](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/blog/author/paudy-heal/ "Posts by Paudy Heal") in [SEO](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/blog/category/seo/)

## How To Get More Accurate Search Volume Data In Google Keyword Planner

You’ll have likely noticed some big changes to the Google Keyword Planner tool recently – namely that it now groups together the search volume data for many similar keyword variants.

For example, if you research ‘car warranty’ and ‘car warranties’ you will see that they each have an estimated average monthly search volume of 8,100. This could be misinterpreted as a total of 16,200 searches for the two keywords collectively, whereas in reality the 8,100 number refers to the volume of both of these variants combined. These changes have been summed up excellently [here](http://www.thesempost.com/googles-keyword-planner-now-combines-keywords-for-search-volume/). There have also been cases of Google suppressing the data for low spending advertisers, as detailed [here](http://searchengineland.com/google-officially-throttling-keyword-planner-data-low-spending-adwords-accounts-255795).

## The Benefits of Obtaining More Granular Keyword Data

Keyword research is an essential activity at various stages of an SEO campaign. Comprehensive research can help to identify a range of new opportunities, and obtaining the most accurate and telling data possible can lead to much more precise forecasting when evaluating the potential traffic opportunities for you or your clients’ websites.

Let’s continue with the ‘car warranty’ and ‘car warranties’ example. The likelihood is that one of variants will be more valuable, be more competitive, and have a higher search volume than the other – but how can we decipher which one now that Google combines the data within the tool?

Take this small sample from a keyword research document, where the new combined data that Google now provides is evident:

![kwp-1](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/Screen-Shot-2016-08-19-at-19.24.28-30x5.png)

Wouldn’t it be far more useful to still have more distinct and clear-cut numbers like the ones below to work from and forecast from instead?

![kwp-2](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/Screen-Shot-2016-08-19-at-19.23.56-30x5.png)

There are a few incredibly quick and easy steps you can take within the Keyword Planner tool that will allow you to see these divided impression numbers, despite the recent update.

## How To Get This Keyword Data

First, click on the arrows next to the all of the keywords you want more specific data for, and this will add them to your plan. Note that the search volumes for these each say 8,100 at this stage. When you’re ready, click on the ‘Review plan’ button:

![kwp-3](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/3-resized-30x10.jpg)

The next page you see should look something like this, minus all of the red boxes of course:

![kwp-4](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/5-resized.jpg)

As you can see by the labels above, there are five things you need to check, adjust, or click in order to get the results you need:

1. Click on the ‘Keyword’ tab
2. Click on ‘Match types’ > ‘All’ > ‘Exact match’
3. Double check that the date range is set to display forecasts by month
4. Enter a bid of £99, as entering a maximum bid will ensure you’re only seeing impressions based on first page results
5. Finally, when you’re ready to go, click on the ‘Get detailed forecasts’ button

Et voila. The table should then update, displaying much more accurate impression data, and providing the average monthly search volumes similar to those you’ve been used to seeing prior to the tool’s update:

![kwp-5](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/6-resized.jpg)

You’ll need to round these numbers up or down to a degree, but you can see that instead of both of these particular keywords having an average monthly search volume of 8,100 each, ‘car warranty’ in fact has approximately 7,300 searches, and the plural ‘car warranties’ has just 800 searches in comparison.

You can now download this data and start to compile keyword research that tells a much more accurate story, as you saw earlier:

![kwp-2](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/Screen-Shot-2016-08-19-at-19.23.56-30x5.png)

I hope this quick guide can act as a handy point of reference next time you perform some keyword research. If you’ve found any alternative ways to discover these more specific numbers within Keyword Planner since its update, let us know in the comments.

## Introduction

Choosing the best search engine optimization tools has become significantly more complex in 2026. Traditional ranking factors now sit alongside AI search visibility requirements, with platforms like Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT Search, and Perplexity reshaping how businesses earn organic traffic. UK companies face intensifying competition across both traditional SERPs and generative search environments, making reliable SEO data essential for informed decision-making. Whether you need keyword research capabilities, technical SEO analysis, or visibility tracking across AI platforms, the right tools directly influence your ability to grow sustainably. This guide evaluates the most effective search engine optimization tools available, explains how to use them strategically, and helps UK businesses determine which investments deliver genuine returns rather than vanity metrics.

## What Are Search Engine Optimization Tools?

**Definition snippet:** Search engine optimization tools are software applications and platforms designed to help businesses research keywords, analyse website technical health, monitor search ranking positions, evaluate competitor strategies, and track organic visibility across both traditional search engines and AI-powered search platforms, enabling data-driven decisions that improve organic traffic performance.

Search engine optimization tools are software platforms that help businesses analyse, monitor, and improve their organic search visibility. These tools provide data about keyword performance, technical website health, competitor strategies, backlink profiles, and search ranking positions that would be impossible to gather manually.

Modern SEO tools range from free browser-based utilities to comprehensive enterprise platforms costing thousands monthly. The most effective tools combine multiple data sources to provide actionable insights rather than raw numbers, helping businesses make strategic decisions about content, technical improvements, and competitive positioning.

### How SEO Tools Support Organic Growth

SEO tools support organic growth by identifying opportunities that human analysis alone would miss. They reveal which keywords drive qualified traffic, which technical issues prevent indexing, and which competitors are gaining visibility in your market space.

For UK businesses investing in [SEO services in London](https://www.dubseo.co.uk/search-engine-optimisation-london/professional-services) and across the country, tools provide the measurement layer that separates strategic optimisation from guesswork. They enable teams to prioritise actions based on potential impact, track progress over time, and demonstrate return on investment to stakeholders.

Effective SEO research begins with understanding which questions your audience asks, which competitors already answer them, and where gaps exist that your content can fill. Tools automate this discovery process and reveal patterns invisible to manual analysis.

### Why SEO Tools Matter More in 2026

The search landscape in 2026 demands more sophisticated analysis than ever. Google's algorithm now evaluates hundreds of signals simultaneously, AI search platforms synthesise information differently from traditional search engines, and user behaviour continues evolving toward conversational and multi-modal queries.

Businesses relying on outdated approaches to SEO analysis find themselves losing ground to competitors using modern tools that account for AI search visibility, entity relationships, and user experience signals. The tools that mattered in 2023 don't necessarily address the challenges of 2026, particularly around generative engine optimisation and zero-click search environments.

Core Web Vitals monitoring, schema markup validation, and entity coverage analysis have all become essential capabilities that modern search optimisation tools must provide.

## Best Search Engine Optimization Tools for Different SEO Tasks

Selecting the right tools requires understanding which SEO tasks matter most for your business. Rather than recommending a single platform, this section evaluates options by function, helping you build a toolkit that matches your specific requirements.

### Keyword Research Tools

Keyword research remains foundational to effective SEO strategy. The best keyword research tools in 2026 combine search volume data with intent classification, competition analysis, and SERP feature identification.

**Google Keyword Planner** provides baseline volume estimates directly from Google's own data, making it essential for initial research despite its limitations around exact volumes. **Semrush** and **Ahrefs** offer comprehensive keyword databases with difficulty scores, trend data, and competitor keyword gap analysis. Both platforms now include AI-generated keyword clustering that groups related terms by intent.

For businesses conducting search engine optimization keyword research on a budget, Google Search Console reveals which queries already drive impressions to your site, providing immediate optimisation opportunities without additional tool investment.

### Technical SEO Analysis Tools

Technical SEO analysis requires tools capable of crawling your website systematically and identifying issues that prevent search engines from properly indexing and ranking your content.

**Screaming Frog** remains the industry standard for technical crawl analysis, identifying broken links, duplicate content, missing metadata, redirect chains, and indexation issues. Its integration with Google Analytics and Search Console data provides context that standalone crawlers lack.

**Google Search Console** itself serves as a primary technical SEO tool, reporting crawl errors, Core Web Vitals performance, mobile usability issues, and indexing status directly from Google's perspective. For comprehensive technical monitoring, businesses should reference our [technical SEO checklist](https://www.dubseo.co.uk/insights/technical-seo-checklist-2026) alongside their tool data.

**Bing Webmaster Tools** provides additional crawl intelligence and is increasingly relevant given Microsoft's integration of AI search capabilities across its ecosystem.

### Rank Tracking Tools

Monitoring website SEO rank positions requires tools that check rankings consistently across locations, devices, and search features. Manual checks are unreliable due to personalisation and localisation.

Effective rank tracking platforms monitor positions daily, track featured snippet ownership, identify ranking volatility, and report on SERP feature visibility including AI Overviews. **Semrush**, **Ahrefs**, and **SE Ranking** all provide robust rank tracking with UK-specific location options essential for businesses targeting local markets.

The most valuable ranking tools now track visibility beyond traditional positions, including presence in People Also Ask boxes, knowledge panels, and AI-generated summaries.

### Content Optimisation Tools

Content tools help ensure your pages satisfy search intent while covering topics comprehensively enough to demonstrate expertise. They analyse top-ranking content and recommend improvements based on semantic coverage gaps.

**Surfer SEO** and **Clearscope** evaluate content against competing pages, suggesting terms, entities, and structural improvements. These tools work best when combined with genuine expertise rather than used as formulaic content generation systems.

For businesses prioritising AI content optimisation, newer tools now evaluate whether content is structured for extraction by AI systems, checking for clear definitions, logical hierarchy, and citation-worthy statements.

### Local SEO Tools

UK businesses serving specific geographic areas need tools that monitor local pack rankings, Google Business Profile performance, citation consistency, and local competitor activity.

**BrightLocal** specialises in local SEO monitoring for UK businesses, tracking local pack positions, managing citations, and monitoring review profiles. Google Business Profile insights provide first-party data about how customers discover and interact with local listings.

Local SEO analysis should include checking NAP consistency across directories, monitoring local keyword rankings, and tracking Google Maps visibility for service-area businesses.

### AI Search Visibility Tools

The newest category of SEO tools addresses visibility across AI search platforms. These tools monitor whether your brand and content appear in AI-generated responses from ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.

Tools like **Profound** and emerging features within Semrush now track AI citation frequency, helping businesses understand their visibility in generative search environments. This category is evolving rapidly, and businesses should evaluate these tools based on coverage breadth and data accuracy rather than marketing claims.

Understanding [how AI search is changing SEO](https://www.dubseo.co.uk/insights/how-ai-search-is-changing-seo-uk-businesses-2026) helps businesses determine which AI visibility tools provide genuine strategic value versus novelty metrics.

## How to Conduct Keyword Research Using SEO Tools

Effective keyword research follows a systematic process rather than random exploration. Here's how to find keywords for SEO using modern tools and methodologies.

### How to Find Keywords for SEO

Finding keywords starts with understanding your business offerings and customer language. Begin with seed keywords that describe your core services or products, then expand using tool suggestions, competitor analysis, and question research.

**A structured keyword research process:**

1. List your core services, products, and topic areas
2. Enter seed terms into keyword research tools (Semrush, Ahrefs, or Google Keyword Planner)
3. Export keyword suggestions and filter by relevance and intent
4. Analyse competitor keywords to identify gaps in your coverage
5. Group keywords by topic cluster and search intent
6. Prioritise based on business value, competition difficulty, and current rankings
7. Map keywords to existing or planned content pages

This process ensures keyword search optimization efforts align with genuine business objectives rather than pursuing high-volume terms with no commercial relevance.

### How to Find Good Keywords

Good keywords balance search volume with achievable competition and clear commercial relevance. The best keywords for your business might have modest search volumes but high conversion potential because they indicate strong purchase intent.

How to find best keywords for SEO involves evaluating:

- **Search intent alignment**: Does the keyword match content you can credibly provide?
- **Competition reality**: Can your domain realistically rank within 6-12 months?
- **Commercial value**: Will ranking drive business outcomes or just traffic?
- **Content feasibility**: Can you create genuinely better content than current results?

Avoid selecting keywords purely based on volume. A keyword generating 50 monthly searches with 10% conversion rate delivers more value than a 5,000-volume keyword with 0.1% conversion.

### How to Search Keywords on a Website

Understanding which keywords a website already ranks for reveals optimisation opportunities without new content creation. Google Search Console's Performance report shows every query driving impressions and clicks to your site.

How to look for keywords on a website involves:

- Reviewing Search Console queries sorted by impressions (not just clicks)
- Identifying keywords ranking positions 5-20 where small improvements yield significant traffic gains
- Checking competitor websites using Semrush or Ahrefs to discover their ranking keywords
- Using site search operator (`site:yourdomain.com keyword`) to find existing relevant pages

This approach often reveals quick wins where existing content needs minor optimisation to capture significantly more traffic.

### Keyword Analysis for SEO

Keyword analysis extends beyond identifying terms to evaluating their strategic value. Comprehensive keyword analysis for SEO includes assessing SERP features, identifying content format requirements, and understanding the competitive landscape for each target term.

Effective analysis reveals whether a keyword requires a blog post, service page, comparison article, or video content. It shows whether AI Overviews dominate the SERP (reducing click-through potential) and whether local intent exists that demands geographic targeting.

## Technical SEO Analysis and Website Performance Monitoring

Technical SEO forms the foundation upon which content and authority strategies succeed or fail. Without proper technical health, even exceptional content struggles to achieve visibility.

### Technical SEO Analysis Essentials

A thorough technical SEO analysis examines crawlability, indexation, site architecture, page speed, mobile usability, and structured data implementation. Tools like Screaming Frog, Sitebulb, and Google Search Console provide different perspectives on technical health.

Essential technical checks include:

- Crawl error identification and resolution
- XML sitemap accuracy and submission status
- Robots.txt configuration review
- Core Web Vitals performance (LCP, INP, CLS)
- Mobile usability compliance
- Schema markup validation
- Internal linking structure analysis
- HTTPS implementation and security headers

Businesses should leverage [data-driven SEO insights](https://www.dubseo.co.uk/data-seo) to prioritise technical fixes based on impact rather than attempting to resolve every issue simultaneously.

### SEO Performance Tracking

SEO performance encompasses more than ranking positions. Comprehensive performance tracking monitors organic traffic trends, conversion rates from organic visitors, page-level engagement metrics, and revenue attribution from search channels.

Google Analytics (GA4) combined with Search Console data provides the most reliable performance tracking for UK businesses. Setting up proper conversion tracking ensures you measure business outcomes rather than vanity metrics like total sessions or bounce rate.

### Website SEO Rank Monitoring

Regular rank monitoring reveals trends that inform strategic decisions. Weekly tracking suffices for most businesses, with daily monitoring reserved for highly competitive keywords or during algorithm update periods.

Effective website SEO rank monitoring includes tracking:

- Core commercial keywords
- Branded search terms
- Long-tail content keywords
- Local pack positions
- Featured snippet ownership
- AI Overview inclusion

### Search Engine Optimization Score Explained

Many SEO tools provide scores or ratings that attempt to summarise website health. SEO scores from tools like Semrush's Site Health or Ahrefs' Health Score indicate the proportion of technical issues relative to total pages crawled.

An SEO rating or score provides useful directional guidance but should never be treated as a definitive quality measure. A site scoring 95% might still have critical conversion issues, while a site scoring 70% might rank exceptionally well for profitable keywords. Scores measure technical compliance, not business performance.

## Free vs Paid Search Optimisation Tools

Understanding when free search optimization tools suffice and when paid investments become necessary helps businesses allocate budgets effectively.

| Factor | Free SEO Tools | Paid SEO Tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Data Depth** | Limited historical data, basic metrics | Comprehensive databases, trend analysis |
| **Keyword Research** | Basic suggestions, limited volume data | Detailed difficulty, intent, SERP analysis |
| **Technical Audits** | Limited crawl capacity (500 URLs typical) | Full site crawls, scheduled monitoring |
| **Rank Tracking** | Manual checks, no automation | Daily automated tracking, location-specific |
| **Competitor Analysis** | Minimal insight | Full competitor visibility mapping |
| **AI Search Monitoring** | Not available | Emerging capabilities |
| **Support** | Community forums | Dedicated account management |
| **Cost** | Free | £80–£400+/month |

### Advantages of Free SEO Tools

Free search engine optimisation tools provide genuine value for businesses beginning their SEO journey. Google Search Console, Google Analytics, and Google Keyword Planner deliver first-party data that paid tools cannot replicate. Free tools like Screaming Frog (up to 500 URLs) and Ubersuggest's limited free tier offer meaningful capabilities without financial commitment.

For small businesses and startups, free seo optimization tools provide sufficient data to make initial improvements and demonstrate early results before justifying paid tool investment.

### Limitations of Free SEO Tools

Free tools typically restrict data volume, historical analysis, and automation capabilities. They rarely provide competitor intelligence, automated monitoring, or the depth of keyword data needed for comprehensive strategy development.

Businesses relying exclusively on free search optimization eventually hit ceiling limitations where manual processes consume more time than paid tool subscriptions would cost. The hidden expense of free tools is the human time required to compensate for their limitations.

### When Paid Tools Become Worthwhile

Paid tools become worthwhile when:

- Monthly organic traffic exceeds 5,000 sessions
- You're competing in moderately to highly competitive markets
- Multiple team members need simultaneous access to SEO data
- You require automated reporting for stakeholders or clients
- Competitor analysis becomes essential for strategic planning
- AI search visibility monitoring matters for your brand

The transition typically makes financial sense when the time saved and insights gained exceed the subscription cost within two to three months.

## Common Mistakes Businesses Make When Using SEO Tools

### Focusing on Metrics Instead of Outcomes

Many businesses obsess over domain authority scores, keyword difficulty ratings, and traffic estimates without connecting these metrics to business outcomes. An SEO tool showing improving metrics means nothing if revenue from organic search remains flat.

Effective SEO tool usage always connects data to [conversion rate optimisation](https://www.dubseo.co.uk/conversion-rate) and business performance rather than treating tool metrics as goals in themselves.

### Ignoring Search Intent

Tools report keyword volumes and difficulty scores but cannot fully evaluate whether your content matches what searchers actually want. Businesses frequently target keywords where their content format mismatches user expectations, leading to rankings without clicks or clicks without conversions.

Always manually review SERPs for target keywords before committing resources to content creation. Understand what Google currently rewards for that query.

### Poor Keyword Selection

Selecting keywords based solely on volume leads to targeting terms where competition is insurmountable or intent doesn't match your offerings. Small and medium UK businesses often achieve better results targeting specific, commercially relevant terms rather than competing for broad industry keywords against established national brands.

### Over-Reliance on Automated Scores

SEO scores and ratings provide directional guidance but frequently mislead businesses into prioritising low-impact fixes. A tool flagging missing alt text on decorative images matters far less than addressing thin content on commercial pages, yet both might appear with equal urgency in automated reports.

## What Most Businesses Misunderstand About SEO Tools

### Why Many Businesses Buy the Wrong SEO Tools

Through years of working with UK businesses, we've observed that tool purchases frequently precede strategy development. Companies invest in enterprise-level platforms before understanding what data they actually need. A business generating 500 monthly organic visits rarely needs a £400/month tool suite designed for agencies managing 50 client websites.

The most common mistake is subscribing to comprehensive platforms and using less than 10% of available features. Start with free tools, identify specific data gaps that limit your decision-making, and invest in paid tools that address those specific gaps rather than purchasing all-in-one solutions prematurely.

### Why Keyword Research Often Fails

Keyword research fails when businesses treat it as a one-time exercise rather than an ongoing strategic process. Tools provide data, but interpreting that data requires understanding your market, competition, and customer journey.

We regularly see businesses targeting keywords where they have no credible expertise, where competition makes ranking unrealistic within reasonable timeframes, or where search intent doesn't match their service offerings. Effective keyword research requires honest competitive assessment and strategic patience rather than chasing every high-volume opportunity.

### Why AI Search Visibility Requires More Than Traditional SEO Software

Traditional SEO tools measure presence in conventional search results. They don't adequately assess whether your content gets cited by ChatGPT, referenced in Perplexity answers, or included in Google AI Overviews.

AI search visibility depends on content authority, entity recognition, and information uniqueness—factors that current SEO tools measure imperfectly at best. Businesses need supplementary monitoring approaches and content strategies specifically designed for generative search environments, which traditional SEO software alone cannot provide.

## How SEO Tools Fit into AI Search Optimisation

### SEO Tools and AI Overviews

Google AI Overviews fundamentally change which content earns visibility for informational queries. SEO tools are beginning to track whether your pages appear within AI-generated summaries, but this capability remains immature across most platforms.

Monitoring AI Overview inclusion requires checking whether your brand, data, or perspectives appear in generated responses. Some rank tracking tools now flag queries where AI Overviews appear, helping businesses understand where traditional organic clicks may be declining.

### Entity-Based Search Visibility

AI search systems prioritise entities—recognised brands, concepts, people, and places—when generating responses. SEO tools that evaluate your entity presence across knowledge graphs and structured data help ensure AI systems recognise and reference your business accurately.

Schema markup validation tools verify that your structured data communicates entity relationships effectively. Google's Rich Results Test and Schema.org validators help ensure technical implementation supports entity recognition across both traditional and AI search environments.

### Search Performance Beyond Rankings

Modern SEO performance extends beyond ranking positions to include citation frequency in AI responses, brand mention sentiment, and information accuracy across platforms. Businesses investing in building topical authority discover that authority signals influence both traditional rankings and AI citation likelihood.

The businesses achieving sustainable search visibility in 2026 use tools to measure holistic presence rather than focusing exclusively on position tracking within traditional blue-link results.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What are the best search engine optimization tools?

The best search engine optimization tools depend on your specific needs. For comprehensive SEO suites, Semrush and Ahrefs lead the market. For technical analysis, Screaming Frog and Google Search Console are essential. For keyword research specifically, Google Keyword Planner combined with either Semrush or Ahrefs provides the most complete data. No single tool covers all requirements, so most effective SEO strategies combine multiple platforms.

### Which SEO tools are free?

Google Search Console, Google Analytics, Google Keyword Planner, Bing Webmaster Tools, and Screaming Frog (up to 500 URLs) are all available at no cost. These free tools provide substantial value for businesses starting their SEO journey, covering technical monitoring, keyword discovery, performance tracking, and basic site auditing without financial investment. Many businesses successfully build their initial organic strategy using only free tools before graduating to paid platforms as competition intensifies.

### How do you conduct keyword research?

Conducting keyword research involves identifying seed topics relevant to your business, expanding them using keyword tools, evaluating search volume and competition metrics, classifying by intent, and mapping keywords to content pages. The process should prioritise commercially relevant terms with achievable competition levels rather than purely high-volume keywords that may never convert into business outcomes. Regularly revisiting your keyword strategy ensures your content remains aligned with evolving search trends.

### How do you find the best keywords for SEO?

Finding the best keywords requires balancing search volume with competition difficulty, commercial intent, and content feasibility. Analyse competitor rankings, review Search Console data for existing opportunities, and evaluate whether your domain can realistically compete. The best keywords often have moderate volumes but strong purchase intent and achievable competition levels for your domain authority. Prioritising long-tail variations often delivers faster results for businesses building authority in competitive niches.

### What is technical SEO analysis?

Technical SEO analysis is the systematic evaluation of website infrastructure elements that affect search engine crawling, indexing, and ranking. This includes checking site speed, mobile usability, crawl errors, XML sitemaps, robots.txt configuration, structured data implementation, internal linking, and Core Web Vitals performance. Regular technical analysis ensures search engines can access and understand your content effectively. Fixing technical issues first ensures content investments achieve their full ranking potential.

### What SEO score is considered good?

Most SEO tools consider scores above 80% as good and above 90% as excellent. However, SEO scores primarily measure technical compliance rather than business performance. A site scoring 75% might generate more revenue from organic search than one scoring 95% if it targets better keywords and converts visitors more effectively. Use scores as directional indicators rather than definitive quality measures.

### Are free SEO tools enough?

Free SEO tools are sufficient for businesses in early growth stages with limited competition. They become insufficient when you need comprehensive competitor analysis, automated daily rank tracking, extensive keyword databases, or team collaboration features. Most businesses competing in moderately competitive markets benefit from paid tools once their organic traffic strategy becomes a primary growth channel. Evaluating your competitive landscape helps determine precisely when upgrading to paid platforms becomes worthwhile.

### Which SEO tools help with AI search visibility?

Dedicated AI search visibility tools are emerging but remain relatively immature. Platforms tracking AI citations include newer entrants alongside evolving features within Semrush and similar established tools. Google Search Console provides some insight through query reports showing AI Overview triggers. Currently, the most reliable approach combines traditional rank tracking with manual monitoring of brand mentions across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity responses.

### How often should SEO performance be monitored?

SEO performance should be monitored weekly for ranking positions and monthly for comprehensive analysis including traffic trends, conversion rates, and competitive movements. Daily monitoring is appropriate only during algorithm update periods or for highly competitive keywords where rapid response provides advantage. Over-frequent checking often leads to reactive decisions based on normal fluctuation rather than meaningful trends. Establishing consistent review schedules with action thresholds helps teams respond to genuine shifts.

### What mistakes should businesses avoid with SEO tools?

The most common mistakes include purchasing overly complex tools before understanding your data needs, focusing on vanity metrics instead of business outcomes, treating automated scores as definitive quality measures, selecting keywords purely by volume without intent analysis, and neglecting to connect SEO data to revenue attribution. Tools should inform strategy rather than replace strategic thinking. Starting with clear objectives before selecting tools ensures your investment directly supports measurable business goals.

## Final Thoughts

Selecting and effectively using the best search engine optimization tools requires understanding both your business objectives and the evolving search landscape. The tools themselves don't generate results—they provide the data and visibility needed to make informed decisions about where to invest optimisation effort.

For UK businesses competing in 2026, the optimal approach combines free tools from Google's ecosystem with targeted paid investments that address specific strategic gaps. Avoid comprehensive enterprise platforms unless your team can genuinely utilise their full capabilities, and always prioritise tools that connect to business outcomes rather than vanity metrics.

The businesses achieving sustainable organic growth use tools to support strategy rather than substitute for it. They combine reliable data with genuine expertise, market understanding, and consistent execution to build search visibility that performs across both traditional and AI search environments.

The answer to this is very subjective and really boils down to which keyword research tool returns enough relevant suggestions for the seed terms you enter.

# The Complete Guide to AI Search Optimisation for UK Small Businesses

23 Jul

Written By [Louize Clarke](https://www.thecuriousacademy.co.uk/blog?author=59fc3cd86f935e363495b59a)

## Why AI Search Optimisation Matters for Your Business Right Now

The digital landscape is experiencing a fundamental shift that's affecting how customers discover businesses online. Traditional Google searches are evolving rapidly, with AI-powered search tools now providing direct answers by synthesising information from multiple websites rather than simply displaying ten blue links.

An estimated 112.6 million people in the U.S. used AI-powered tools in 2024, and this trend is accelerating globally. In the UK, businesses are increasingly finding that their potential customers are asking AI tools questions like:

• "What's the best digital marketing course for small businesses in Reading?" • "Where can I find affordable web design services near Reading?" • "How do I improve my restaurant's online visibility?"

Google displays a Search Generative element for 86.83% of all search queries, making AI-driven search the norm rather than the exception. This represents a massive opportunity for forward-thinking businesses to establish themselves as authoritative sources before their competitors catch on.

**The competitive advantage:** Most businesses haven't adapted their websites for AI search yet. By implementing these strategies now, you'll position yourself ahead of competitors who are still focused solely on traditional SEO approaches.

## Understanding AI Search: How It Differs from Traditional SEO

Traditional SEO focused on ranking for specific keywords to appear in search results. AI search optimisation (also called AIO, GEO, or AEO) focuses on being cited, referenced, and recommended by AI tools when they generate responses to user queries.

Think of it this way: instead of trying to be the top result for "digital marketing courses Reading," you want AI tools to recommend your course when someone asks, "What's the most comprehensive digital marketing course for beginners in Reading?"

### How AI Search Engines Process Information

AI search engines work differently from traditional search algorithms. They understand conversational language and can interpret natural questions whilst providing contextual answers. Unlike traditional search, they synthesise multiple sources, combining information from various websites to create comprehensive responses.

They also prioritise authority and trust, favouring content from established, credible sources, and consider recency - fresh, updated content often receives preference in AI responses.

Many AI systems have tight timeouts (1-5 seconds) for retrieving content, so website speed and accessibility are crucial factors in whether your content gets included in AI responses.

## The Three Types of AI Search Results Your Business Can Appear In

Understanding how your business can appear in AI search results helps you tailor your optimisation strategy effectively.

**Direct Citations and References** This occurs when AI tools specifically mention your business or website as a source of information. For example, if you run a digital marketing agency and have written comprehensive guides about social media strategy, an AI tool might cite your website when someone asks about effective Instagram marketing techniques.

Research shows that Perplexity, in particular, is more likely to cite sources than other platforms and includes both images and video content, making it especially valuable for businesses with visual content.

**Featured Business Recommendations** AI tools can recommend specific businesses that match user requirements. This is particularly valuable for local businesses and service providers. When someone asks, "Who offers the best SEO training in Reading?" you want your business to be among the recommendations.

**Conversational Follow-up Suggestions** As users engage in longer conversations with AI tools, your business might be suggested in follow-up responses. This creates opportunities for deeper engagement and higher-quality leads.

Important insight: When people click to a website from search results pages with AI Overviews, these clicks are higher quality, where users are more likely to spend more time on the site. This means the traffic you receive from AI search is often more valuable than traditional search traffic.

## Setting Realistic Expectations: The Current State of AI Search Traffic

Before diving into optimisation strategies, it's crucial to understand the current landscape. Recent analysis found that AI search was driving less than 1% of traffic to most websites as of June 2025, with many seeing numbers below 0.5%.

However, this doesn't diminish the importance of AI optimisation for several reasons:

• **Early adoption advantage:** You're establishing authority before the space becomes saturated • **Quality over quantity:** AI tools now account for about 10% of some sites' traffic, with Perplexity delivering both the highest volume of traffic and the best conversion rates • **Future-proofing:** AI search usage is growing exponentially • **Compound benefits:** Many AI optimisation techniques also improve traditional SEO performance

## Step 1: Ensure AI Accessibility and Technical Foundations

Before AI tools can recommend your business, they need to be able to access and understand your website effectively. Page loading speed should aim for under 3 seconds, as many AI systems have tight timeouts for retrieving content. Your website must work perfectly on mobile devices, and clean HTML structure is essential since many AI crawlers don't handle JavaScript well.

**What to implement immediately:** • Submit your website to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools • Ensure your Google Business Profile is complete and current • Check your website's loading speed using Google PageSpeed Insights • Verify that your contact information is consistent across all pages

Clear titles, descriptions, dates, and schema.org markup help AI systems quickly understand your content, so these technical foundations are non-negotiable for AI search success.

## Step 2: Master Conversational Content Optimisation

The way people search with AI tools is fundamentally different from how we use traditional Google search. Instead of typing keywords, users ask complete questions in natural language.

For example, instead of the traditional keyword approach of "Digital marketing courses Reading small business," users now ask AI tools complete questions like "What are the most effective digital marketing courses for small business owners in Reading who want to learn social media advertising and SEO?"

**Implementation strategy:** • Write content that directly answers complete questions • Use natural, conversational language throughout your website • Include location-specific information for local businesses • Address user intent, not just keywords

This shift means your content needs to sound like something a knowledgeable person would say in conversation, not a keyword-stuffed webpage trying to game search algorithms.

## Step 3: Implement Strategic Content Structure

If you're explaining a complex or multi-step process, use numbered steps and clear transitions between each part. This makes it easier for AI systems to pull out individual steps when someone asks for specific instructions.

Your content structure should follow a logical hierarchy. Use main headings (H1) for your primary topic, such as "Complete Guide to Facebook Advertising for UK Small Businesses." Follow with key subtopics as H2 headings like "Setting Up Your Facebook Business Manager," then specific aspects as H3 headings such as "Creating Your First Ad Campaign."

**Best practices for AI-friendly structure:** • Use descriptive headings that could stand alone as questions • Place the most important information at the top of each section • Include clear transitions between topics • Use bullet points and numbered lists for complex processes

This structured approach helps AI tools understand your content hierarchy and extract relevant information when answering user queries.

## Step 4: Create Comprehensive FAQ Sections

FAQ sections are particularly valuable for AI optimisation because they directly match how people ask questions to AI tools. These sections should analyse customer service enquiries for common questions and use Google's "People Also Ask" feature for additional question ideas.

**Strategic FAQ development approach:** • Include questions about pricing, process, timing, and location • Provide complete, helpful answers rather than brief responses • Address follow-up questions that naturally arise • Use conversational language that mirrors how people actually speak

Here's an example of an AI-optimised FAQ for a digital marketing course:

**Q: How long does it take to complete your digital marketing certification?** **A:** Our comprehensive digital marketing certification typically takes 12-16 weeks to complete when studying part-time (8-10 hours per week). The course is designed for working professionals, so you can progress at your own pace. Full-time students often complete the programme in 6-8 weeks. The course includes practical assignments, case studies, and a final project that demonstrates your ability to create and execute digital marketing campaigns.

This approach provides AI tools with detailed, contextual information they can use to answer related questions comprehensively.

## Step 5: Optimise for Long-tail and Conversational Keywords

Traditional SEO taught you to target specific keywords, but AI search requires focusing on long-tail keywords that align with conversational queries and natural language processing. The keyword strategy has evolved significantly.

Where traditional approaches focused on terms like "SEO course," AI-optimised content targets phrases like "How to learn SEO for small business websites in Reading." Advanced AI optimisation goes even further, addressing questions such as "What's the best way to improve Google rankings for a local restaurant in Reading?"

**Implementation tactics:** • Stop filtering out keywords with low search volumes - you need to map more terms with lower monthly searches than historically • Focus on semantic search by using related phrases, synonyms, and natural language variations • Identify conversational queries from Google's People Also Ask, AnswerThePublic, and forum discussions on Reddit • Include question-based content that mirrors how people actually speak to AI assistants

This approach ensures your content aligns with how people naturally interact with AI tools, increasing your chances of being cited in responses.

## Step 6: Maintain Content Freshness and Authority

Some AIO studies have found that AI search responses tend to prioritise citing websites that are recently updated. Regular updates signal to AI tools that your content is current and reliable, which is particularly important in fast-moving industries like digital marketing.

Your content maintenance strategy should include updating pricing, services, and business information monthly. Add new case studies, testimonials, or examples quarterly, and refresh statistics and data points regularly to maintain accuracy.

**Authority building activities:** • Publish original research or industry insights • Create detailed guides that demonstrate expertise • Include specific examples and case studies • Reference credible sources and link to authoritative websites

Building authority isn't just about fresh content - it's about demonstrating genuine expertise through comprehensive, well-researched material that other sites want to reference and link to.

## Step 7: Build Brand Recognition and Citations

Some research suggests that a strong, regularly referenced brand makes your website more likely to be cited in AI overviews and chatbot responses. This is similar to how traditional search tends to prioritise recognisable brands because they're more likely to provide trustworthy information.

Brand building strategies should focus on encouraging customer reviews and testimonials, participating in industry discussions and forums, and seeking opportunities for media coverage or expert commentary. Developing partnerships with other reputable businesses and creating shareable, valuable content that others want to reference builds the kind of authority AI tools recognise.

**Citation building tactics:** • Publish valuable resources that other websites want to link to • Participate in industry surveys or research studies • Contribute expert opinions to relevant publications • Engage in professional networking within your industry

The goal is to become recognised as a thought leader in your field, which naturally leads to more citations and references from both human authors and AI systems.

## Step 8: Create In-depth, Authoritative Content

Google wants to show content that fulfils peoples' needs. Focus on making unique, non-commodity content that visitors from Search and your own readers will find helpful and satisfying. This means going beyond surface-level information to provide genuine insights and practical value.

Content depth strategies should include developing comprehensive guides that cover topics thoroughly, including practical examples and step-by-step instructions, addressing common challenges and providing solutions, and incorporating visual elements like images, diagrams, or videos to support text content.

**Content types that perform well in AI search:** • **How-to guides:** Step-by-step instructions for common tasks • **Comparison articles:** Detailed comparisons between options or approaches • **Case studies:** Real examples of successful implementations • **Industry insights:** Original analysis or commentary on industry trends • **Problem-solution content:** Identifying challenges and providing practical solutions

This comprehensive approach ensures AI tools have substantial, valuable content to draw from when answering user queries in your subject area.

## Step 9: Implement Schema Markup and Structured Data

Schema markup helps AI systems quickly understand your content by providing structured information about your business, services, and content. Essential schema types for businesses include organisation schema for basic business information, local business schema for location-based businesses, service schema for service providers, and FAQ schema for question-and-answer content.

Implementation can be achieved through WordPress plugins like Yoast SEO or RankMath for automated schema generation. Ensure consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) information across all platforms, and include business hours, service areas, and payment methods where applicable.

**Technical implementation tips:** • Use WordPress SEO plugins for automatic schema generation • Manually implement schema for unique business types • Test your schema markup using Google's Rich Results Test • Monitor search console for structured data errors

This technical foundation helps AI tools categorise and understand your business type, making it more likely to be recommended for relevant queries.

## Step 10: Monitor and Measure AI Search Performance

Organisations should focus on what can be concretely measured - AI crawler and agent visits, referral traffic from AI search platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and others, and citations in AI-generated answers.

Key metrics to track include referral traffic from AI platforms, time on site and engagement metrics for AI-referred visitors, conversion rates from AI search traffic, and brand mentions in AI responses through manual monitoring.

**Monitoring tools and techniques:** • Google Analytics for tracking referral traffic sources • Google Search Console for understanding search performance • Manual testing by asking AI tools questions related to your business • Setting up Google Alerts for your brand name and key topics

Regular monitoring helps you understand which content performs best in AI search and refine your strategy accordingly.

## Industry-Specific AI Optimisation Strategies

**For Educational and Training Businesses** Digital marketing course providers, training organisations, and educational institutions should focus on creating comprehensive curriculum overviews that AI can easily parse. Develop detailed course descriptions with learning outcomes, include instructor credentials and expertise areas, provide clear information about certification processes, and create comparison guides between different course options.

**For Professional Services** Agencies, consultants, and professional service providers should emphasise detailed service descriptions with process explanations, case studies demonstrating expertise and results, team credentials and industry experience, client testimonial integration throughout the website, and clear pricing and package information where appropriate.

**For Local Businesses** Restaurants, shops, and location-based services should prioritise complete Google Business Profile optimisation, location-specific content and service area descriptions, local keyword integration in natural conversational contexts, customer review integration and response strategies, and event and promotion information with regular updates.

## Common Pitfalls to Avoid in AI Search Optimisation

Over-optimisation and keyword stuffing remain problematic because AI tools can detect unnatural language patterns. Focus on writing for humans first, ensuring that your content flows naturally and provides genuine value.

Neglecting traditional SEO fundamentals can lead to negative consequences from Google's broad core updates. AI optimisation should complement, not replace, fundamental SEO practices that have proven effective over time.

**Additional pitfalls to avoid:** • Focusing solely on traffic volume instead of engagement quality • Ignoring mobile and technical performance requirements • Creating content without considering user intent • Failing to update and maintain existing content regularly

Success in AI search comes from balancing technical optimisation with genuine value creation for your audience.

## Your 90-Day AI Search Optimisation Implementation Plan

**Days 1-30: Foundation Building** Complete a technical audit and fix any loading speed issues. Set up Google Search Console and verify website accessibility. Update your Google Business Profile with comprehensive information, create or enhance your primary FAQ section, and begin monitoring current search performance metrics.

**Days 31-60: Content Optimisation** Audit existing content and add conversational elements throughout your website. Implement proper heading structure across key pages, develop 3-5 comprehensive guides relevant to your expertise, create detailed service or product descriptions, and begin building internal linking structure between related pages.

**Days 61-90: Authority and Expansion** Publish additional in-depth content pieces that demonstrate thought leadership. Implement schema markup across relevant pages, develop customer testimonial and case study sections, begin outreach for brand mentions and citations, and establish a regular content update schedule to maintain freshness.

This systematic approach ensures you build a solid foundation before advancing to more sophisticated optimisation techniques.

## Measuring Success: Key Performance Indicators for AI Search

Success in AI search optimisation requires monitoring different metrics than traditional SEO. Primary success indicators include engagement quality metrics like time on site, pages per session, and bounce rate, alongside conversion performance through lead generation, enquiry quality, and sales attribution.

Brand visibility becomes increasingly important, measured through mentions in AI responses and citation frequency. Traffic quality from AI platforms and subsequent user behaviour provides insights into the effectiveness of your optimisation efforts.

**Secondary indicators to monitor:** • Content performance - which pages get cited most frequently • Search visibility improvements in traditional search rankings • Authority signals including inbound links, social shares, and brand searches • Technical performance improvements in page speed and crawl efficiency

Regular monitoring of these metrics helps refine your strategy and focus efforts on the most effective optimisation techniques for your specific business and audience.

## The Future of AI Search: Preparing for What's Next

The AI search landscape continues evolving rapidly. In 2025 and beyond, AI agents won't just passively suggest information—they'll actively make decisions on behalf of people. Emerging trends include increased personalisation in AI search results, growing importance of visual content in AI responses, expansion of voice search and conversational queries, and integration of AI search with e-commerce and booking systems.

**Future-proofing strategies:** • Continue focusing on helpful, authoritative content creation • Maintain technical excellence and fast loading speeds • Build genuine expertise and thought leadership in your field • Stay informed about AI search developments and adapt accordingly

The businesses that adapt early to these changes will have significant advantages as AI search becomes more prevalent and sophisticated.

AI search optimisation represents a significant opportunity for UK businesses willing to adapt their digital presence thoughtfully. The key is understanding that this isn't about gaming algorithms—it's about making your website genuinely helpful to people seeking your products or services.

Start with these immediate actions: audit your website's technical performance and fix any speed issues, create or enhance your FAQ section with conversational, helpful answers, update your Google Business Profile with comprehensive, current information, and begin incorporating natural, conversational language into your content.

Success in AI search comes from consistently providing value to your audience. Focus on answering their questions thoroughly, demonstrating your expertise clearly, and maintaining current, accessible information about your business.

The businesses that thrive in the AI search era will be those that genuinely serve their customers' needs while adapting to new technologies. By implementing these strategies systematically, you'll position your business to benefit from this fundamental shift in how people discover and evaluate businesses online.

Your competitive advantage lies in starting now, before AI search optimisation becomes standard practice. The opportunity exists today for forward-thinking businesses to establish themselves as authoritative sources in their industries and capture the high-quality traffic that AI search platforms provide.

Good keyword research is the foundation for any SEO strategy. This guide aims to teach you how to do keyword research like a pro.

## Why is Keyword Research Important?

2026 update: volume-first keyword selection was the standard approach in 2019, intent-first prioritisation is what works in 2026, especially with roughly 68% of Google searches now ending without a click (SparkToro/Datos, up from about 58.5% in 2024). Picking keywords on search volume alone, without checking whether that volume converts into visits, matters more than ever.

Keyword research is crucial to any [SEO campaign](https://exposureninja.com/blog/definitive-seo-guide-for-business-owners/). If you pick the wrong keywords or focus on none at all, you might as well be shouting at a brick wall while your customers walk the other way.

If you put the time into your keyword research, you’ll see much better returns on the time, effort and money you’ve invested in creating content to draw potential customers to your website.

It could also give you the edge over [your competitors](https://exposureninja.com/blog/seo-competitor-analysis/), so **wins** all around!

## How Many Keywords Should You Have?

Your list of keywords and phrases can get out of hand fast when you’re doing keyword research.

We suggest having a final list of between **25 and 50 keywords and phrases** to optimise various website pages for or create content based around.

It’s likely you’ll come across a lot of keywords in your research, so it’s wise to use a keyword tool, such as [Semrush\*](http://thankyouninjas.com/), to help you identify how much **value** the keywords will have.

You should also take **search intent** into consideration. If you put your keyword into a search engine and all the results are very informational, or unrelated to your business offering, then that keyword might not be for you.

We’ve broken the whole keyword research process down into bite-size steps that will help you with your research, no matter your skill level.

## Step 1 – Make a List of Topics Related to Your Business

Creating a list of topics related to your business is the best place to start with keyword research.

Think of the types of **services** you offer. For example, if you run a gardening business, your topics may include;

- Gardening
- Landscaping
- Lawnmowing
- Hedge cutting

We now have four gardening related keywords that can be used to find even more related terms. It’s a great place to start, as you don’t have to get too technical with it.

You can use [this spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1cx4eKLBlgKocVqat8J6QdMAMN3-PXP7BTVLnZprjduo/copy) to help you keep track of your keywords.

You’re likely to find **four different types** of keywords, all based on the searcher’s intent.

We call these search intent keywords (very original) and they fit into the following categories:

1. Informational
2. Commercial
3. Transactional
4. Navigational

2 and 3 are sometimes bundled together as Commercial.

![](https://exposureninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Seach-intent-funnel-v3.png)

Commercial and Transactional keywords could be things like “ _hire a gardener_” or “ _landscaping services_“.

Informational searches are things like “ _how to stop grass going yellow_” or “ _how to cut hedges_”

A navigational search is one where someone knows where they want to go, for example typing “ _Amazon_” into Google as they want to visit the Amazon website, or searching “ _Facebook Login_” because they want to view the Facebook login page.

You might be thinking, “ _Well, I don’t need to worry about navigational searches, people will only use them to head straight to my site._”

While this is true, it’s also true that competitors may run ads on searches related to your brand name so they can try and grab those heading to your site via a search engine. Make sure you know the type of navigational searches people may be making when they are heading to your website.

Using questions that your customers ask as **key phrases** or **long-tail keywords** can help you create content that helps answer these questions. This is an ideal way to build a relationship with your customers, as well as to guide them towards a purchase.

You can start this process by making a list of the most common questions your customer ask you on a regular basis. Do they often ask you to compare two products? Do they ask how long your type of work takes?

Sticking with the gardening example, they may ask questions such as “ _How long does it take a garden to be landscaped?_” or “ _How often do I need to hire a gardener?_”

There are also **online tools** you can use to find questions your customers may ask.

Long-tail keywords earn their place here too. Backlinko’s analysis of 306 million keywords found that 91.8% of all search queries are long-tail (though these make up only around 3.3% of total search volume, so they’re about matching intent precisely, not chasing big numbers). They’re also widely reported to convert at roughly 2.5x the rate of shorter, broader terms, worth prioritising for local and niche searches especially.

## Step 7 – Analyse Your Keywords

Now we have this hefty list of keywords, we need to find out which ones are **worth targeting**. There are several factors we need to look at when deciding which keywords to keep and which to throw.

The main factors we’ll be looking at are:

- **Search volume** – so we know if the keyword is getting the right amount of traffic
- **Keyword Difficulty** – so we know how difficult it will be to compete for the top stop on Google for this keyword
- **Cost Per Click (CPC)** – to give us an idea of how many ads are being run on this search term
- **Traffic Location** – to make sure we’re reaching searchers in the right countries

Add a fifth factor for 2026: intent match. A keyword can have great volume and low difficulty and still be the wrong keyword, if the searches behind it aren’t actually looking for what you offer. Score each keyword against how closely the intent behind it matches your page or service, not just against volume and difficulty, and be wary of chasing volume alone: with roughly 68% of searches now ending without a click, a lot of that volume never reaches a website at all.

We’ll be using [Semrush\*](http://thankyouninjas.com/) for this step.

We have 24 keywords for this example, but you may have found more or less for your business. We recommend ending this process with **25 – 50 keywords in total**. We’re just keeping it small here for example’s sake.

In Semrush, we start by adding all the keywords into the keyword manager. We can see the **volume of searches per month** for each keyword, the **cost per click**, the **keyword difficulty** (listed here as KD%) and some other metrics that we won’t worry about today. You can also filter by location – you don’t want to be targeting keywords that perform well in the USA if you won’t be offering your service there.

![A screenshot of the keyword manager in Semrush](https://exposureninja.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Screenshot-of-the-keyword-manager-in-Semrush.png)

_A screenshot of the keyword manager in Semrush_

We can start using the above metrics to **prioritise** specific keywords, and potentially **remove** others.

Add the data for each keyword into your spreadsheet. Many tools allow you to download a CSV. file with all the data.

Once you’ve added the data for all your keywords, you will have a better idea of which ones are getting the right amount of traffic.

You don’t want to target keywords getting tens of thousands of searches per month, as you’ll likely get **lost** in the crowd.

You also don’t want to target keywords that might be getting no searches. That said, if you are targeting local keywords or are in a **niche industry**, you may have more low volume keywords that are being searched by customers who are ready to make a purchase, or as they’re known in the industry, low-hanging fruit.

Just because they are low doesn’t mean they are not worth targeting, but you should understand why the search volume is low.

Highlight the keywords that are in the **midrange**, not too high and not too low. The high end and the low end will be different for every business, and for this example, 100 monthly searches is the low end, and 12,000 is the high end.

![Screenshot of the Google search results for “Garden designers Nottingham”](https://exposureninja.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Screenshot-of-Google-results-for-garden-designers-nottingham-1.png)

_Screenshot of the Google search results for “Garden designers Nottingham”_

Right away, we can see that there are **multiple ads** on this search term taking up a lot of room at the top of the results. Looking at our table, [Semrush\*](http://thankyouninjas.com/) predicts that these ads are costing $1.26 per click.

It’s good to take a look at the **type of ads** that are running – are they for **services** or **products**? If we were seeing mostly gardening product ads for this search, we may have to reconsider the intent behind the search, and if our service fits in here. Luckily, these ads are for garden design services, so that’s a good indication that our service does fit here.

Moving onto the organic search results, we can see that most of the results here are for garden design companies and landscapers. As we are offering these services, this is exactly the type of search term we will want to target.

Google has decided this is a more _commercial_ keyword – meaning when someone types it in they are looking for a service or researching their options when it comes to making a decision.

Let’s take a look at a higher volume keyword, “ _landscaping_“, and see if the search intent is different.

![Screenshot of Google search results for “Landscaping”](https://exposureninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Google-search-results-for-landscaping-map-pack.png)

![Screenshot of Google search results for “Landscaping”](https://exposureninja.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Google-search-results-for-landscaping.png)

_Screenshots of Google search results for “Landscaping”_

These search results have a more _varied_ intent.

Right at the top is a map pack, which is ideal for local businesses. Even if the rest of the “blue link” search results are more informational results, for example, the Wikipedia page for landscaping, the map pack shows that many people searching for “ _landscaper_” are doing so to look at local landscapers.

It’s important to keep the type of results that come up for a search in mind when choosing keywords. Think about whether people searching for this term are looking for a definition, inspiration or to actually make a purchase.

If they’re looking for inspiration, you could [create a piece of content](https://exposureninja.com/blog/rank-top-of-google/) based around popular trends. if they’re looking for information, create a page on your site that gives them that information in a fun and interesting way.

Once you’ve identified the category that these searches fall into, you can move on to the next step and start **prioritising** your keywords.

![](https://exposureninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Keyword-categories.png)

_Screenshot of the keyword sheet with the category added to each keyword_

### Prioritising Your Keywords

Now that you have several viable keywords and understand the intent behind each search now is the time to **prioritise** them. We’d suggest selecting **10 priority keywords** to start, with a mixture of different search intents and search volumes.

It’s also worth deciding if these keywords are **short, medium, or long term SEO goals**. Higher volume keywords are often more long term keywords, whereas searches around trends may be short term.

If you already have a website set up and want to optimise existing pages for some of these keywords, include the URL in the sheet. If you [haven’t got a website](https://exposureninja.com/services/website-development/) just yet, you can make a note of the type of pages you want to rank for each term, whether that’s the homepage, a product or service page, or a blog post.

Once you’ve started to fill in these parts of the sheet, here’s an example of how that might look:

![A screenshot of the keyword research spreadsheet with more information filled in](https://exposureninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/keyword-spreadsheet-complete.png)

_A screenshot of the keyword research spreadsheet with more information filled in_

This list is not static and will evolve with your business as well as current trends. It’s good to revisit it on a quarterly or every 6 months to make sure you’re still targeting the best keywords for your company. With time and practice, you’ll be able to see what works for your business and what doesn’t.

## **Step 8 – Use AI Prompt Keyword Research (New for 2026)**

Alongside Google, people are now searching directly inside ChatGPT and Perplexity, and the keywords (or more accurately, prompts) they use there don’t always match the ones they’d type into Google.

A quick way to start: search your top 10-15 keywords as natural-language questions in ChatGPT Search and Perplexity, and note which of your competitors get cited in the answer for each one. If a competitor keeps showing up in AI answers for a keyword you’re not targeting at all, that’s a gap worth adding to your list.

This also creates a natural next step once your keyword list is built: our [guide to AI search optimisation](https://exposureninja.com/services/ai-search-optimisation/) covers how to turn these keywords into content AI tools will actually cite.

## **Keyword Research FAQs**

### **What is keyword analysis?**

It’s the process of evaluating the keywords you’ve found, by search volume, difficulty, cost per click and intent, so you can decide which are actually worth targeting, covered in Step 7 above.

### **What’s the difference between keyword research and keyword analysis?**

Keyword research is finding keywords. Keyword analysis is evaluating and prioritising the ones you’ve found. This guide covers both: Steps 1-6 are research, Step 7 is analysis.

### **How many keywords should I target per page?**

Usually one primary keyword with two or three closely related secondary keywords per page, rather than trying to rank one page for a long list of unrelated terms.

### **What are the best free keyword research tools?**

Google Keyword Planner, Google Search Console, and Also Asked’s free monthly searches are all solid starting points before you need a paid tool like Semrush or SE Ranking.

### **What is keyword intent?**

It’s what the searcher actually wants: information, comparison, purchase, or a specific website. Matching your content to that intent matters more than matching the keyword’s exact wording.

### **How often should I do keyword research?**

Revisit your keyword list every quarter to every 6 months, search behaviour, competitors, and your own business all shift over that timeframe.

## **What SEO Actually Does For Your Business**

When someone searches for what you do, they're ready to buy. They're not browsing. They're looking for someone to call. If your business isn't showing up, that customer is going to your competitor instead.

SEO fixes that. It puts your business in front of people who are already looking for you, at the moment they're ready to make a decision. And unlike paid ads, the results compound over time. The longer you do it, the stronger your position gets.

The same applies to AI search. When someone asks ChatGPT "who's the best plumber in Leeds" or "which accountants work with tradespeople", the answer comes from a small set of websites the AI trusts. We make sure yours is one of them.

## **Getting Found On AI Search**

The way people search is changing fast. Instead of typing keywords into Google, they're asking ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity natural questions and getting a single answer back.

That answer comes from a handful of websites. The sites that get picked are the ones with clear structure, authoritative content, proper schema markup, and answers to the questions people actually ask.

Most SEO agencies are still optimising for 2019. We optimise for both: Google rankings AND AI search visibility. It's one of the most important changes in search in twenty years, and it's happening now.

Your monthly report tracks both.

## **SEO: Grow Faster With Our Search Engine Optimisation Service**

We work with small businesses across the UK who are serious about growing through search.

Tradespeople, consultants, health and wellness businesses, coaches, retailers, and professional services. If your customers are searching for what you do, on Google or on AI, and you're not showing up, we can help.

Frequently Asked Questions

### Still Got _Questions?_

Everything people ask before signing up. If anything is missing, ask on your strategy call.

How long does SEO take to show results?

Most clients see meaningful movement within 60 to 90 days. Some keywords move faster depending on competition and where you're starting from.

We always set honest expectations before we begin.

Do I need to do anything once we start?

Very little. We handle everything. Occasionally we'll need a quick answer or access to something, but the day-to-day runs without you needing to be involved.

Is £297 a month all I pay?

Yes. There are no setup fees, no hidden extras, and no long-term contract. You pay monthly and can stop at any time.

What if my website is old or poorly built?

We'll flag anything that needs addressing as part of the initial review. Sometimes a website needs work before SEO will be effective, and we'll be upfront about that from the start.

Can you guarantee I'll rank number one?

No ethical SEO agency can guarantee specific rankings. What we guarantee is consistent documented work, full transparency, and a monthly report that shows exactly what's happening.

Will this work for my type of business?

SEO works for any business with customers who search online before they buy or enquire. Tradespeople, professionals, clinics, coaches, accountants, agencies.

If your customers are searching, we can help you get found.

How It Works

## Our SEO Process

Here is exactly what happens when you work with us.

1

We Start With a Conversation

Before anything else, we get on a call to understand your business, your market, and what you actually want SEO to do for you. More calls, more enquiries, more of the right customers finding you online. We need to understand the goal before we look at a single page.

2

We Run a Full SEO Audit

We go through your website properly. Technical issues, page speed, broken links, missing meta data, duplicate content, indexing problems. Most websites we look at have several things quietly holding them back in Google. We find them all before we start fixing anything.

3

We Identify Your Keywords

We work with you to establish which keywords matter most for your business. What are your customers actually searching for? What terms are your competitors ranking for? We build a keyword map that connects the right search terms to the right pages on your site.

4

We Review Your Existing Pages

We go through your current website content page by page. Are your service pages optimised for the right terms? Is the copy doing a job for Google as well as your visitors? We look at titles, headings, structure, and content quality across the whole site.

5

We Look at Your Backlinks

Backlinks are one of the strongest signals Google uses to rank websites. We review your current backlink profile to see what is pointing at your site, what quality those links are, and where the gaps are compared to your competitors. This shapes part of our ongoing strategy.

6

We Build Your SEO Plan

Everything from the audit, keyword research, page review, and backlink analysis feeds into a clear plan. What gets fixed first, what new content gets created, and what link building activity we will run each month. You know exactly what we are doing and why.

7

We Optimise Your SEO and Add Content Every Month

We work through the plan month by month. Optimising existing pages, fixing technical issues, building new keyword-relevant content, and growing your backlink profile. SEO is not a one-off job. It compounds over time, and we are in it with you for the long term.

8

Monthly Report and Review

Every month you get a clear report showing your keyword rankings, traffic trends, and what work was completed. No jargon. Just a straightforward picture of where you were, where you are now, and what is coming next.

## Understanding SEO Pricing in the UK

SEO pricing refers to the way consultants, agencies, and freelancers charge for SEO services. Prices vary depending on the complexity of your website, the level of competition in your industry, geographical locations that you are targeting and the scope of work involved.

In the UK, monthly SEO services pricing can start from as little as £300 for smaller local campaigns, rising to over £10,000 for large-scale or multi-site strategies. The wide price range reflects differences in service depth, required expertise and campaign scale.

## What to Consider When Looking at SEO Pricing

The decision to invest in SEO services should be based on your specific business goals and resources. If you’re a local business looking to attract nearby customers, even a modest investment in [**local SEO**](https://www.polarisagency.com/seo/local-seo-services/) can yield significant returns. For e-commerce sites or international businesses, you can expect an SEO retainer to cost more. Consider your current online visibility, your competition’s SEO efforts and your growth targets when deciding on your SEO investment. When evaluating SEO packages and pricing, consider both your immediate needs and long-term goals.

## SEO Costs in the UK and the Different Types of SEO Providers
